text: Seeds split two ways. In endospermic, or albuminous, seeds the endosperm stays in the mature seed as the food store, and the cotyledons stay thin: maize, wheat, rice, castor and coconut. In cereals, the aleurone layer secretes alpha amylase on germination to digest the starch.
